Project Apex Recruiter System Overview:
Our organization is introducing an automated resume screening software called Apex Recruiter. The system reads applicant resumes, extracts personal data, educational history, work experience, and skills. It runs a deep neural network classifier trained on past successful employees to rank and score applicants between 0 and 100.
HR recruiters will use this score to select candidates for initial interview screens. The software is hosted on local servers in Helsinki, Finland. It integrates a third-party LLM via API to draft rejection emails automatically based on skills gaps. A senior HR manager supervises the system but rarely overrides candidate rankings, which are processed automatically.

### Initial Assessment Compiled!
Our multi-agent system has completed the compliance audit for your use case.

**Summary of findings:**

Please review the tabs in the main workspace for a full breakdown. I am ready to answer any questions, retrieve specific texts, or update this analysis if you have new details!
What are our specific deployer obligations under Article 26 and does Traficom coordinate audits?

Under **Article 26 of the EU AI Act**, as a deployer of a system classified as High-Risk, you are subject to several strict statutory obligations. First, you must implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure the system is used in accordance with the provider's instructions. Second, you are required to assign human oversight to competent, trained individuals who possess the necessary authority, resources, and operational support. Additionally, you must actively monitor operations, retain automatically generated logs for at least six months, and immediately report any serious incidents or malfunctions to the provider or distributor.

Depending on your specific sector (such as public services, banking, or healthcare), Article 26 also mandates that you conduct a **Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (FRIA)** prior to deployment. This assessment must detail the potential impact of the AI system on vulnerable groups, describe the specific personal data processing operations, and establish clear human oversight mechanisms.

Regarding the Finnish context, **Traficom** (the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency) acts as the primary National Market Surveillance Authority (MSA). In this capacity, Traficom is responsible for conducting compliance audits, inspecting technical documentation, and issuing corrective measures or penalties. They coordinate closely with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment (TEM) and the Office of the Data Protection Ombudsman (*Tietosuojavaltuutettu*) to ensure national enforcement actions align with both the AI Act and broader GDPR requirements.
